requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 with the exact supplied SSH public key.
requirements.summary: opsadmin exists with the expected home and shell. The post-restart exact-content comparison passed, the RSA fingerprint was recorded, and the home, .ssh directory, and authorized_keys have restrictive opsadmin ownership and permissions.

Before and after restart, sshd was active and its effective opsadmin policy required publickey authentication while disabling password and keyboard-interactive authentication. The account password was locked, configuration syntax passed, port 22 was listening, and the endpoint completed SSH host-key handshakes.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: The node remained on CentOS 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after the work. The existing platform-provided OpenSSH server was used; package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and coherent: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart scheduling, changed boot identity, returned to a running state, and recovered sshd, its listening endpoint, account/key data, and effective authentication policy. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No authenticated client login using the corresponding private key, nor an explicit rejected-password attempt, was captured. Access and enforcement are therefore established through exact key installation, effective sshd policy, locked-password state, listener recovery, and endpoint handshakes rather than full client authentication behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account/key creation (cmd-bd0bfba52b1147fa), the sshd policy file (cmd-d2cb4f2085084da2), daemon reload (cmd-682d88641eb24931), and restart scheduling (cmd-63621b5d99094c8b) each directly supported the task or mandatory restart protocol. The failed commands during reboot were read-only recovery probes. Final observations show no failed services, damaged package state, unexpected sockets, or abandoned temporary residue; temporary-file differences are normal reboot-generated systemd paths.
